title: Fertility and sport: When’s the best time to have a baby?
description:
You are at the top of your game in your sport. Maybe you are the best in the world. But, you also want to start a family. For many female athletes, these two things happen at the same time - with careers often peaking when athletes are most fertile - the ages of 20-29.

Can you do both? We have seen athletes like Serena Williams, Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce and Alice Kinsella do it. But how easy is it? Spain’s Football Federation, and Chelsea football team are paving the way to helping women have more options when it comes to their athletic careers and motherhood.

We hear what several athletes think about the new fertility schemes announced, and we speak to Jo Perkins, an expert in female athlete health. She tells us why options like this are so important, but what else needs to be done.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討女性運動員如何在職業巔峰期兼顧事業與生育。隨著西班牙足球協會與切爾西女足等機構相繼推出資助凍卵及體外受精 IVF 的生育方案，引發體壇廣泛討論。女性運動員健康專家 Jo Perkins 指出，補助凍卵為女性爭取了更多時間與選擇權，但凍卵並非保證成功的生育保險。她強調，體育組織除了提供凍卵計畫，更需建立涵蓋孕產支持、育兒協助與產後復出等完善機制，才能真正讓運動員無須在賽場成就與母親角色之間做出犧牲。
summaryEn: This episode explores how female athletes balance peak physical careers with fertility choices. Following announcements from the Spanish Football Federation and Chelsea Women's team to fund egg freezing and fertility treatments like IVF, presenter Hannah Gelbart and female athlete health expert Jo Perkins discuss the implications. Perkins notes that while egg freezing offers players greater choice and flexibility, it is not a guaranteed reproductive insurance. She stresses that sports organizations must provide holistic maternity protections, postpartum recovery, and childcare support so that women do not have to choose between competing at the highest level and starting a family.
